transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Um… I guess it’s mostly that I’ve been kind of slowed down lately. Not in a dramatic way, I don’t think, but at work my hands feel like they’re moving through glue. Like sectioning hair or mixing color takes me way longer than it used to, and people have started noticing I’m just… slower. I’m trying to keep up, but it’s been hard.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days I wake up with this heavy, flat kind of sadness in my chest. It’s like… I’ll think about the life I was trying to build, and it just feels hard to see the point in trying. Is that what you mean?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with people?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I mean, I still show up and do what I’m supposed to, but I’m not really the same with people. I used to talk a lot with clients, help the newer stylists when they were stuck, and I’d go hiking with friends sometimes. Now I mostly just keep my head down and try to get through the day. It’s not that I don’t care about them… I just don’t really have that spark in me lately, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling more tired or low on energy lately, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I don’t want to say yes if I’m just being lazy or something. I notice I’m slower, but as far as being tired when I’m not doing much… I guess I haven’t really paid attention to it that way. Sorry, is that an okay answer?
Have you noticed that you feel tired or have a lack of energy most days, even when you’re not doing anything physically strenuous?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I mean, I get through work and everything, so I don’t want to say I’m exhausted all the time if that’s not accurate. I guess I haven’t noticed it clearly enough to say most days. Is that okay?
Have you noticed that things that used to make you happy or give you pleasure, like spending time with friends or doing things you used to enjoy, don’t seem to do that anymore?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I still go to work and I’m polite and everything. But stuff that used to feel good just kind of… doesn’t hit the same.

Like I used to chat with clients a lot, help the newer stylists when they needed it, and I’d go hiking with friends sometimes. Now I mostly keep my head down and avoid people more than I used to. It’s not like I hate anyone or anything… I just don’t really have that spark in me lately. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that you feel tired or low on energy most days, even when you’re not doing anything physically hard?

I’m sorry, I know you’ve asked that a couple times. I just… I don’t think I can say for sure. I don’t really track my energy like that.

I’m tired after work, but that feels normal, because I’m on my feet and talking to people. On days where I’m not doing much, I guess I haven’t noticed it enough to say it’s most days. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like work, hobbies, or spending time with people?

Completely lost interest… I don’t know if I’d say completely, because I still show up to work and I can do what I need to do. But yeah, it’s definitely less than it used to be.

I used to talk more with clients, help the newer stylists, and I’d go hiking with friends sometimes. Lately I mostly just keep my head down and avoid people more. It’s not that I don’t care at all, I just… don’t really have that spark in me right now. Is that what you mean?
Would you say that most days, you feel down or sad for most of the day, even if it's not extremely intense?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m crying all day or anything, because I’m not always visibly upset.

But most mornings I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness in my chest. Like… this feeling that there’s not really a point in trying to build the life I thought I was working toward. It’s not always dramatic, but it’s there a lot of the day. Does that answer it right?
Would you say that you no longer get pleasure or satisfaction from things you used to enjoy, like work, hobbies, or spending time with friends?

Yeah… I think I get less out of those things now. I don’t want to say I get nothing from them, because that sounds kind of extreme, and I can still do my job.

But I used to chat with clients more and help the newer stylists without really thinking about it. And I used to go hiking with friends sometimes. Lately I mostly just keep my head down and avoid people more, not because anyone did anything wrong… I just don’t really have that spark in me. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, including things you used to enjoy like work, hobbies, or being with friends?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say almost all like I’m completely shut off from everything, because I can still go to work and get through the day.

But it’s definitely changed. I used to enjoy talking with clients more, and I’d help the newer stylists, and I used to go hiking with friends sometimes. Lately I mostly just keep my head down and avoid people more. It’s not that I’m trying to be rude or anything… I just don’t really have that spark in me right now. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you've lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even those you used to enjoy like work, hobbies, or being with friends?

Yeah… I think I’ve kind of answered this before, but yes, it’s still true. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t enjoy anything at all, because I can still show up and function.

But things I used to naturally care about just feel harder to connect with. I used to chat with clients more, help the newer stylists, and I’d go hiking with friends sometimes. Now I mostly keep my head down and avoid people… not because I dislike them or anything. I just don’t really have that spark in me like I used to. Is that okay to say?
Would you say that you feel tired or low on energy most days, even when you’re not doing anything physically hard?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do get tired sometimes, but I haven’t really been tracking whether it’s most days or anything like that.

I can still get through work, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But… maybe I have been lower energy than usual? I’m not sure if that counts. What do you mean by low energy exactly?
Would you say that you’ve lost pleasure or joy in almost all activities, including those you used to really enjoy like work, hobbies, or spending time with friends?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I do nothing or that I’m totally checked out, because I still go to work and I try to be normal.

But I used to actually enjoy chatting with clients, and helping the newer stylists felt nice. And I used to go hiking with friends sometimes. Lately I mostly just keep my head down and avoid people more. It’s not that I don’t care about them… I just don’t really have that spark in me right now. Is that what you mean?
Would you say that you feel tired or low on energy most days, even when you’re not doing anything physically hard?

I’m not sure I can say “most days” confidently. I mean, I do feel kind of drained sometimes, even if I haven’t done anything huge, but I also still get myself to work and do what I’m supposed to do.

So… maybe my energy isn’t great, but I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really been keeping track. Is that an okay answer?
Would you say that you've been having trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions, more so than usual?

Yeah… a little, I think. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do my job, because I can, but there are times I’m looking at color formulas or the appointment screen and my brain just kind of blanks.

Then I’ll second-guess really simple things I used to do automatically, which is embarrassing. I usually figure it out, but it takes me longer than it should. Does that count as trouble concentrating?
Would you say that you feel tired or low on energy nearly every day, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

I don’t know if I’d say nearly every day. I mean… I get tired, but I also don’t want to make it sound like I’m just exhausted all the time.

Some days I feel kind of worn out even if work wasn’t that busy, but I haven’t really been tracking it closely. So maybe it happens, but I’m not sure it’s nearly every day. Is that okay to say?
Would you say that you have trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions nearly every day?

Nearly every day… I’m not totally sure. But it does happen a lot where I’ll be looking at color formulas or the appointment screen and my brain just kind of blanks for a second.

Then I start second-guessing things I usually know how to do without thinking, which makes me feel kind of stupid, honestly. I can usually get through it, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… yeah, concentrating has been harder. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that you have completely lost pleasure or interest in almost all activities, including those you used to enjoy, nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d say completely lost, because that sounds really dramatic… but it’s definitely changed.

I used to be more chatty with clients, and I liked helping the newer stylists, and I’d go hiking with friends sometimes. Lately I mostly just keep my head down and try not to deal with people more than I have to. It’s not that I hate everything, I just… don’t feel that spark in me the way I used to.

Does that count, or are you asking if I literally enjoy nothing at all?

inference_history.note: The patient described a subjective slowing of physical and mental processes, which could indicate a depressive episode, persistent depressive disorder, or another mental disorder. No differential has been ruled out yet.

The patient endorsed slowed movement and a persistent low mood, which supports the consideration of major depressive disorder subtypes. No significant features pointing to other categories (e.g., psychotic, bipolar, or organic disorders) were mentioned, so the list remains focused on depressive disorders.

The patient continues to endorse persistent low mood, diminished interest or pleasure in activities they previously enjoyed, and psychomotor slowing. They do not clearly endorse significant fatigue or low energy independent of physical activity, which has not solidified enough to rule out or confirm specifiers related to energy level. However, the core symptoms of depression are present and meet criteria for at least a moderate depressive episode. The list has removed F32.0, F32.9, F33.0, and F33.9 as the clinical picture has become clearer.
